design.quote: cross-sectional analyses from three national dietary surveys

population.quote: Intake of ultra-processed foods in Sweden and its association with diet quality and weight status: cross-sectional analyses from three national dietary surveys
population.value: adults, adolescents, and young children in Sweden

sample_size.quote: Data were derived from the three most recent Swedish national dietary surveys: Riksmaten (RM)-Adults (2010-2011; n = 1797), RM-Adolescents (2016-2017; n = 3099), and RM-Young Children (2021-2024; n = 1820).

intervention.quote: Intake of ultra-processed foods in Sweden and its association with diet quality and weight status

primary_findings.quote: each 10 E% increment in UPF corresponded to 0.61% higher BMI (95% CI: 0.04-1.18; p = 0.036)
primary_findings.outcome: BMI change per 10% increase in UPF

primary_findings.quote: The prevalence of overweight or obesity was higher in the top versus bottom tertiles of UPF intake after energy adjustment (PR = 1.16; 95% CI: 1.03-1.30; p = 0.018)
primary_findings.outcome: Prevalence ratio of overweight/obesity top vs bottom tertiles of UPF intake
